title: MealOS — Kitchen Line Map
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity native Android product direction comp
Primary request: Design one full-screen MealOS cooking-mode interface for the recipe “Garlic-herb chicken + baby potatoes + broccoli” in serving mode “Dinner + lunch tomorrow.”
Scene/backdrop: one native Android app screenshot only, no device frame or bezel; canvas represents a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra unfolded at 2504 × 2256 pixels, near-square landscape, with a subtle central vertical hinge-aware gutter.
Style/medium: exceptionally polished high-fidelity Android UI, modern Material 3 behavior beneath a distinctive “Kitchen Line Map” visual grammar. Midnight-blue enamel ground; crisp porcelain-white labels; scarlet, amber, cobalt, and herb-green route inks. Adult, disciplined, tactile, highly readable, production-designed rather than conceptual.
Composition/framing: equal-weight two-pane layout split around the vertical hinge. A slim adaptive navigation rail at far left with clear icons and labels: “Today”, “Plan”, “Recipes”, “Grocery”; Today selected. Left pane is the current action, prominently labeled “Step 2 of 5”, with the recipe title and serving mode visible, a large direct instruction for the current station, and a compact next-step preview. Right pane is an operational station list of ingredients plus two prominent live timers. Maintain generous safe padding around the hinge and screen edges. Use 48dp minimum touch targets and clear native Android hierarchy.
Core visual system: a disciplined schematic route line using only 45-degree and 90-degree segments connects four labeled stations in order: “Prep”, “Air fry”, “Rest”, “Serve”. Make current and next state unmistakable through line weight, filled station nodes, restrained glow, and Material 3 state treatment. The route is integrated into the working interface at useful scale; do not shrink an entire network into a tiny overview.
Exact visible text, rendered verbatim and legibly:
“MealOS”
“Today”
“Plan”
“Recipes”
“Grocery”
“Garlic-herb chicken + baby potatoes + broccoli”
“Dinner + lunch tomorrow”
“Step 2 of 5”
“Air fry the potatoes”
“Shake the basket halfway through”
“Next: Add the chicken”
“Prep”
“Air fry”
“Rest”
“Serve”
“Ingredients”
“Chicken thighs”
“Baby potatoes”
“Broccoli”
“Garlic”
“Fresh herbs”
“Olive oil”
“Potatoes”
“12:48”
“Chicken”
“08:20”
“Pause”
“Add 2 min”
Interaction details: two large timer modules on the right, potatoes timer reading exactly 12:48 in amber and chicken timer reading exactly 08:20 in scarlet, each with obvious Pause and Add 2 min controls. Ingredients appear as a highly legible station list with practical completion indicators, not generic cards. Include restrained Android system status/navigation treatments only if they fit naturally.
Color palette: midnight-blue enamel background, porcelain white typography, route accents in scarlet red, amber yellow, cobalt blue, herb green; high contrast and accessible.
Materials/textures: subtle enamel depth and fine surface grain, otherwise clean flat native UI; no photoreal food imagery.
Constraints: exactly one full-screen app surface; balanced equal-weight panes; hinge-aware layout; current and next cooking states immediately understandable; large readable text; realistic spacing; 48dp targets; designed operational app surface.
Avoid: device bezel, phone render, hands, decorative poster, generic recipe cards, tiny overview map, illegible filler, lorem ipsum, invented nutrition claims, invented health claims, invented performance claims, excessive gradients, glassmorphism, dense dashboard chrome, desktop web styling, warped typography, duplicate labels, decorative food photography, branding other than MealOS.
